q_occupation.text: Does the arrangement grant occupation/use of premises for a term against rent, licence fee, premium or deposit (as opposed to a bare personal permission with no occupation)?
q_occupation.legal_test: Karnataka Stamp Act Art 30 covers 'Lease of immoveable property including an under-lease or sub-lease and any AGREEMENT TO LET or sub-let'. Karnataka has NO separate leave & licence article (unlike Maharashtra's 36A); an occupation-conferring licence is charged as a lease/agreement-to-let under Art 30.

q_exclusive.text: Is exclusive possession granted (right to exclude the grantor), indicating a true lease rather than a licence?
q_exclusive.legal_test: Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. R.N. Kapoor, AIR 1959 SC 1262. In Karnataka both a lease and an occupation licence are charged under Art 30, so the duty is the same; the distinction still matters for other legal consequences and for s.6 where a competing description exists.

grey_bare_licence.reason: A bare licence conferring no occupation may fall outside Art 30 (potentially an Art 5 agreement). Classification is uncertain and duty-affecting — escalate and recommend adjudication rather than defaulting to the lease article.

source.ref: Karnataka Stamp Act 1957 Art 30 ('any agreement to let'); Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. R.N. Kapoor, AIR 1959 SC 1262; s.6
source.quoted_text: Art 30 charges a lease 'including ... any agreement to let or sub-let'. Karnataka has no distinct leave & licence article; an occupation licence is charged as a lease under Art 30. Both terminals resolve to KA-ART30-lease — the duty is identical, so the classification here is confirmatory rather than duty-splitting (contrast Maharashtra Art 36 vs 36A).

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH. Documents that Karnataka charges L&L as a lease (Art 30) — both terminals point to KA-ART30-lease. The meaningful escalation is the bare-licence-no-occupation grey zone. Contrast the MH tree, where the split is duty-determinative (Art 36 vs 36A).
